Why It Matters Defence ministry money flowing into a civil battery-electric aircraft developer shows dual-use funding becoming a route for electric aviation startups to finance work that private capital alone has been slow to back.

Elysian Aircraft, a Dutch aerospace startup developing battery-electric aircraft technologies, has closed a pre-Series A round raising over €6 million in equity , alongside more than €6 million in public funding . The investors include venture capital firm FideFlux, defence-focused investor SecFund and ROM InWest, the regional development agency of the Dutch province of North Holland, as well as individual investors and family offices. SecFund's investment was made through funds provided by the Dutch Ministry of Defence. The round follows a technology programme awarded by the Ministry to a consortium co-led by Elysian and the Netherlands Aerospace Centre (NLR), focused on technologies for next-generation unmanned aircraft. Including earlier rounds, the company has raised over €20 million in private and public funds in total.

Founded in 2023 by Daniel Rosen Jacobson, Rob Wolleswinkel and Reynard de Vries, Elysian is headquartered in Hoofddorp near Amsterdam. It is building the technology stack needed to make large-scale battery-electric aircraft commercially viable. Its core product is the E9X, a battery-electric passenger aircraft designed to seat around 90 people and fly up to 1,000 km. Citing a 2025 CE Delft study, the company says battery-electric propulsion incurs 18% energy loss, versus 65 to 81% for alternatives such as hydrogen fuel cells or e-SAF. Unlike eVTOL startups targeting urban air taxis with two-to-four-seat aircraft, Elysian is aiming at the mainstream short-haul market, designed to support existing regional airline networks. It also pursues defence applications through partnerships with TU Delft, NLR and Fokker Services Group, among others.

Wouter Lammerse, co-founder and General Partner of FideFlux, said the company exemplifies the ambitious European deep tech innovation the firm looks for. Ernst Coolen, Investment Director at SecFund, said Elysian's technology could accelerate sustainable civil aviation and has clear potential for future defence applications, including unmanned systems. Rosen Jacobson, co-founder and co-CEO, said the company will use the coming months to deliver technical, commercial and financial milestones ahead of a Series A in 2027. The new capital will go toward advancing Elysian's core aviation electrification technologies, addressing the technical hurdles of battery-electric flight and broadening their application across commercial and defence markets.

Dowty, a GE Aerospace company, will open a UK Innovation Centre backed by £19 million from GE Aerospace to speed development of propellers and Open Fan technologies.

Embraer Services & Support CEO Carlos Naufel outlined the company's global aftermarket strategy, citing new Component Pool Program agreements with Austrian Airlines for 13 E195s and Air Dolomiti for 30 E-Jets.

The FAA certified the Boeing 737 MAX 7 on August 3, a jet about six feet four inches longer and 22,500 lb heavier at maximum takeoff weight than the 737-700 it replaces.

Goodwin co-founder Tolga Demirel says AI will strengthen relationship-focused private jet charter brokers rather than replace them, while brokers competing mainly on lowest price will face a harder path.

Honeywell Technologies and Keppel's Infrastructure Division announced a collaboration to expand low-carbon fuel production across Asia-Pacific, covering SAF, renewable diesel, methanol-to-jet fuel and biocrude upgrading pathways.

SkyDrive has signed a comprehensive partnership with Kyushu Electric Power to explore integrating eVTOL aircraft into urban development and community planning in Japan, targeting service entry in 2028.

A study by Miao et al. (2026) finds that at about $80 per short ton, U.S. farmers, especially in the South, could profitably supply biomass for 3 billion gallons of SAF per year.

Air India and Airbus have signed a feasibility study agreement to develop India's first voluntary corporate Sustainable Aviation Fuel programme, which remains at the study stage.

Tecnam has appointed Estonia-based Diamond Sky as its authorized dealer for Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, adding the company to its global network and giving it the full Tecnam range.

Direct2, a Bend, Oregon air operator also trading as Beeline UAS, joined Matternet's network of Part 135 drone delivery operators in 2026, alongside Ameriflight and UPS Flight Forward.

FlyWith, an invitation-only app for sharing private charter flights and splitting costs, says several hundred Members have joined since its September launch, completing a growing number of shared flights.

Aero Ventures describes its AI aircraft valuation platform as a self-reinforcing data flywheel, modelled on Zillow's Zestimate, but it faces thin transaction volume in a market of only hundreds of $10 million-plus deals a year.

Florida's Doroni Aerospace has raised more than $60 million from over 20,000 investors for its H1-X flying vehicle, with advanced test flights planned to begin in 2027.

Skyports CEO Duncan Walker said the first two of four Dubai vertiports are built and certified, with $70–80 million deployed and the company funded entirely by equity for now.

A ClimateTech series installment profiles five firms pursuing aviation decarbonization, with Infinium's Texas eSAF plant, expected online in 2027, targeting 23,000 tonnes per year of mainly SAF.

Poseidon Aerospace cut aerodynamic database development from eight months to three weeks using Flexcompute's GeometryAI and Flexcompute Flow, announced Nov. 17, 2026.

Indian Oil Corporation has secured government approvals to commercially supply sustainable aviation fuel from its Panipat refinery, which can meet India's 1 per cent SAF blending target for international flights in 2027.

The U.S. Air Force's AFWERX has awarded Virginia-based Electra a $4.7 million contract to help develop the EL9, a nine-seat hybrid-electric aircraft, and evaluate its potential military use.

Textron's Citation Longitude, certified by the FAA in September 2019, offers 3,500 nm range and a long cabin, but 25 deliveries in 2025 trail the Latitude's 47.

Envision Energy and IATA signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on power-to-liquid electric sustainable aviation fuel, starting with a jointly published research report on eFuels and eSAF.

An opinion piece urges UK travel technology buyers to fund reliable journey-connection handling before dedicated air-taxi integrations and to treat aerial access as a bounded trial.

Tecnam appointed Leonardo Falanga Head of Technology and Innovation in September and is rolling out AI across production, documentation and parts traceability, with certified people keeping final sign-off.

Archer Aviation and Formula 1 announced a multi-year partnership to bring the Midnight eVTOL aircraft to select Grand Prix events across the US, Middle East, Asia and Europe.

Pratt & Whitney Canada unveiled its PT9 turboprop at NBAA-BACE with Transport Canada certification in hand, claiming 33% more power at altitude and 20% lower fuel burn, but no aircraft application.

EFISCharts.com launched an FAA chart subscription service for Dynon SkyView and Advanced Flight Systems displays, with annual plans starting at $39 for VFR coverage and $49 for combined VFR and IFR.

Cirrus Aircraft received a Type Certificate for the composite SR22 in 2000, and within two years the Continental IO-550-N-powered single-engine piston became the best-selling general aviation airplane.

SOAR AI reported quarterly revenue up 245% and $41.2 million in cash, with roughly $1.2 billion of AI infrastructure business under contract following its September merger with Alignment Engine.
